Expenditure Framework was originally adopted in April 2018 and

April 2020, March 2021, July 2022 (Mid Suffolk),October 2022

Expenditure Framework required the production of a CIL Expenditure
Programme for each District and contained decisions for Cabinet to
make or note on CIL Bids for CIL expenditure. These decisions
relating to the expenditure of CIL monies form one of the ways in
which necessary infrastructure supporting growth was
delivered.

identified in Appendix A of the Framework for CIL Expenditure
report provided to Cabinet’s on the 5th and

workshops with the Joint Member advisory panel. Members adopted the
original Framework documents set out in paragraph 1.1  of the report by Council decision in April 2018.

purpose:
To agree and approve Mid Suffolk Town Centre
Business Improvement Fund
content:
It was
RESOLVED: -
 
That
Cabinet:
 
1.1         
That Cabinet noted and endorsed the proposed
changes to the Stowmarket Shopfront Grant scheme, including the
proposal that up to £200,000 of the existing Stowmarket
shopfront allocation may be used to supplement the district wide
scheme.

 
1.2         
That Cabinet noted and endorsed the alignment
between the new Business Improvement Fund and the Mid Suffolk Rural
Support Fund.

 
1.3         
That delegated authority be given to the Director
of Place, in consultation with the Head of Economy & Business
and the Portfolio Holder for Thriving Communities to approve any
future changes to scheme criteria, guidance or
processes.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
To
increase take up and impact of the scheme by allowing internal
improvements and addressing known barriers such as business cash
flow.
 
To
provide a flexible, responsive approach that enables timely support
for applicants.
 
To
create a coherent, district wide business support programme that
aligns multiple funding streams, including the Mid Suffolk Rural
Support Fund.
 
To
ensure the Council’s investment delivers greater value,
improved business resilience, enhanced accessibility, and increased
footfall across towns and villages.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Option A – Do Nothing (Not Recommended)
Retain the current Shopfront Scheme restricted to external
works.
·      
Does not address low take?up
·      
Does not enable businesses to undertake essential
internal improvements that support accessibility, sustainability,
and growth.
·      
Limits alignment with wider Mid Suffolk
scheme.
Option B – Make Limited Adjustments Only (Not
Recommended)
Minor tweaks (e.g., promotional uplift), without broadening scheme
eligibility.
·      
Insufficient to stimulate additional
applications.
·      
Does not create flexibility regarding match
funding.
·      
Does not enable integration with the Mid Suffolk
Rural Support Fund.
Option C – Approve Full Scheme Amendments
(Recommended)
Convert to a district?wide Town & Village Centre Business
Improvement Fund to provide grants for both internal and external
works, greater match?funding flexibility, and delegated authority
for future changes.
·      
Supports business resilience, sustainability,
customer experience and productivity.
·      
Enables use of the Stowmarket allocation to support
a district?wide offer, supplementing the Mid Suffolk Rural Support
Fund to enable more businesses to be supported District
wide.
·      
Addresses low uptake and barriers to
participation
 
Any Declarations of Interests Declared: None
Any Dispensation Granted: None

content:
It
was RESOLVED: -
 

1.1         
That Cabinet reviewed and noted the summary of
Round 2 proposals coming forward, outputs and evaluation
outcomes.
 

1.2         
That Cabinet resolved to approve from the
Stowmarket Town Centre Gateway Fund upper funding limits
of:
 
(a) 
£100,000 towards the Mid Suffolk Voluntary
Organisations Forum (MSVOF) led redevelopment of Lockington Road
(former fire station) - which also supported the expansion of Red
Gables existing services and facilities based at Ipswich
Street;
(b) 
£100,000 towards the conversion of 6 Old
Fox Yard to create design room, improved gallery space and workshop
including kitchenette/accessible facilities - led by Stowmarket
Arts CIC;
(c) 
£70,000 towards supporting the
establishment of a new coffee roastery and related community
activities in the town delivered by Good Vibes Coffee Ltd (subject
to a suitable unit or space being identified in the town centre
locality); and
(d) 
£80,000 towards supporting the
establishment of a new milkshake, ice cream and dessert venture by
two local entrepreneurs (subject to a suitable unit or space being
identified in the town centre locality)
 

1.3         
That Cabinet delegated authority to the Director
of Place to finalise the terms and conditions of grant funding
agreement with the beneficiaries, and subject to any suitable
controls, monitoring and legal advice for ensuring key objectives
and purposes of the grant scheme are secured.
 
 
REASON FOR DECISION
To maximise the Council’s
opportunities to directly invest in Stowmarket’s high street
and wider town?centre
area - utilising the Gateway 14 dividend - to reduce vacancy rates,
stimulate investment, and generate new activity and additionality
at key locations.
 
To develop and promote a
diverse range of potential business, cultural, heritage, tourism,
hospitality and other end?uses that help address the town’s economic and social challenges,
and which complement existing plans and pipeline initiatives for
Stowmarket
 
Alternative Options Considered and Rejected:
Do Nothing. Not recommended.
The Council’s £1.5m high street and town centre fund
(STCGF) investment package for Stowmarket’s high street and
town centre requires transparent reporting of outcomes to date. Any
high impact/above threshold expenditure items needed to be formally
considered and approved, if appropriate, by Cabinet as a key
strategic decision and in line with the funding
framework.
 
That Round 2 (STCGF) summary
and support specific requests for (conditional) funding approvals
be noted by Cabinet. Recommended.

Interests Declared: None

To
endorse the 24/25 Mid Suffolk Greenhouse Gas Report

It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1         
That, the contents of the Annual Climate Report
for 2025 and the GHG Emissions report 2024/25 at Appendix A of the
report, be noted by Cabinet, prior to publication on the
council’s website.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
In
reviewing the progress towards our net zero commitments for council
and area wide emissions the Cabinet would be provided with a more
in depth understanding of the work taking place across council
services. This will enable Members to review the progress being
made in reducing carbon emissions and consider the available
options and their trade-offs, the factors that affect
decarbonisation, and the challenges and opportunities going
forward.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
To
provide the most recent Climate and Greenhouse Gas Emissions
reports so that Cabinet can track progress related to the climate
emergency.
 
To
not provide an update on the annual Climate report and Greenhouse
Gas Emissions report. This option was not recommended

purpose: To Note the Q4 Performance Report
content:
It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1         
That Cabinet noted the performance for Q4 for
25-26, including the key performance indicators that are shown as
red in the status and commentary around these.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
To
ensure overview of Council performance and areas of focus where
performance was not where it was expected to be, and mitigation
measures to address any KPIs below agreed targets.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Option 1: No reporting on council performance – not
pursued as good governance required regular review of performance
against council objectives and statutory duties.
 
Option 2: Reporting on statutory performance requirements only
– not pursued as performance was wider than just the
Council’s statutory duties, it also entailed the priorities
identified in the Mid Suffolk Plan.
 
Option 3: Reporting on Key Performance Indicators and connected
actions that are 80% or greater complete – currently the
option pursued for Q4 performance reporting.
 
Option 4: Reporting on Key Performance Indicators and progress
on the Council’s agreed strategies, connected to actions
identified from risk mitigation – not pursued at present, but
as shown in the report below performance reporting is under
development and will change moving forward into future
quarters.
 
Any Declarations of Interests Declared: None
Any Dispensation Granted: None

A.

report);

The transfer of £2.250m to the Mid Suffolk
Plan Implementation reserve in addition to the budgeted amount of
£2.383m for the surplus in the financial year.
b) 
The transfer of £165k from the Pooled Funds
reserve to fund the loss on sale of the Schroder
Fund.
c)  
The transfer of £203k from the Homelessness
reserve to fund costs incurred in the financial
year.
d) 
The transfer of £976k of EPR income to the
Waste Reserve to fund the new waste services in
2026/27.

The transfer of £3.1m to the Mid Suffolk
Plan Implementation reserve in addition to the budgeted amount of
£2.9m relating to the dividend received from Gateway 14
Ltd.

Procurement and S151 Officer in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Finance & Resources to make final changes to the
reserve transfer subject to items identified through the Statement
of Accounts preparation and audit.
 
1.4.That

2026 in Appendix B.
 
1.5.That
Cabinet noted the capital programme spend of £23.318m for
2025/26 and the associated capital financing in Appendix
C.

purpose:
To approve and agree the Review
of Housing Options for climate positive living scheme
content:
To approve and agree the Review
of Housing Options for climate positive living scheme
 

It was
RESOLVED: -
 
That
subject to receiving planning consent:-
 
1.1         
That Cabinet agreed to proceed with Option 3,
market and dispose of the land on the open market with the benefit
of planning consent for sustainable homes.
 
1.2         
That Cabinet approved to undertake the demolition
of the existing bungalows and prepare the site for development
ahead of any sale.
 
1.3         
That the appointment of demolition contractors
and any associated consultants be delegated to the Director for
Property, Development and Regeneration in consultation with the
Portfolio Holder for Housing and Property.
 
1.4         
That the negotiation and completion of the sale
of the land be delegated to the Director for Property, Development
and Regeneration in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Property and Housing and Property.
 
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
To
enable the site to be marketed with a planning consent in line with
the Council’s brief, and for the Council to undertake the
demolition to help unlock the site for the development of new
high-quality homes which meet the council’s aspirations for
climate positive homes that are truly sustainable.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Option 1- MSDC
deliver the scheme
Subject
to achieving planning consent this option would see 5 market homes
delivered on the site to replace the 6 existing bungalows. The
brief of the project was to provide homes which met the
Council’s aspirations of low carbon homes which promoted
sustainable, climate positive homes by decarbonising the built
environment. This would create a legacy project for the Council to
raise aspirations in the local area of building to a high standard
whilst bringing the whole life carbon of the home to near zero, by
using bio-based construction materials. This not only had a
positive impact on the environment, but it also created a
sustainable home to live in due to the reduction of cost on utility
bills, utilising technologies such as solar panels and air source
heat pumps combined with a fabric first approach utilising modern
methods of construction and bio-based materials.
The
scheme had been designed to meet the brief described above and a
planning application was being prepared for submission.
The team
have assessed delivering the 5 homes as market homes or as
affordable homes. To replace the existing dwellings with affordable
housing was not viable, and the location did not lend itself to
affordable housing due to poor public transport links and lack of
amenities.
The
locality of the area and the landscape of the existing properties
within the area, leant itself to redevelopment of market homes.
This would be a unique offer within the market currently and
provide sustainable homes for those who had both a focus on
environmental and economic sustainability.
To
deliver the scheme, the land would need to be transferred to the
General Fund to enable market homes to be delivered.
This
option had been discounted due to development risk attached to the
delivery of a market led scheme to the Council.
Option 2-
Regeneration of the existing dwellings
Condition
surveys had been completed on the properties by an asset surveyor
within the Council. The reports concluded that the properties were
at the end of their economic life, and that the properties would
require extensive works both internally and externally to bring
them to a modern lettable standard, but that this would not
fundamentally improve the fabric of the buildings and therefore the
performance or liveability for residents.
The
properties had also had asbestos surveys completed which identified
areas of asbestos within the properties which would require removal
and rectification by specialists which would be a significant cost
given it would be required to 6 properties.
This
option had been discounted as it was not financially viable or
practicable.
Option 4-Do nothing

 
This
was not a viable option. The properties state of disrepair would
increase over time along with the impact this had on the wider
community and the cost implications to the HRA of being void and
the failure to use this site for beneficial purpose.
 
Any Declarations of Interests Declared: None
Any Dispensation Granted: None

1.2         
That Cabinet approved an increased upper funding
allowance for delivery of the planning approved modular-build
café, toilet block and changing place facility as
re-estimated by an independent cost consultant in December 2025,
and shown at Confidential Appendix B.
 
1.3

modular-build café, toilet block and changing place
facility.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
Belle?Vue Park was a significant asset for the Council, the
people of Sudbury, and the wider district. Its upkeep and
enhancement delivered a range of benefits, including increased
footfall and usage, greater opportunities for healthy activity and
wellbeing across all age groups, improved safety and security,
strengthened community pride in place and local heritage, and
better connectivity and visibility with the wider town. Investing
in the improvements outlined in this report demonstrated the
Council’s continued commitment to securing these positive
outcomes.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Do
Nothing. Not recommended. The Council remains committed to continue
investing in affordable improvements to the park for the benefit of
the local community, visitors and wider town. This includes public
realm, play, security, accessibility and facilities
enhancements.
 
Option 2. Not recommended (due to constraints of time, re-design
and planning process). Create an alternative toilet/café
kiosk/changing place scheme for delivery by March 2028.

cost recovery
content:
To
consider increases to parking charges to move the service to full
cost recovery

It
was RESOLVED: -
 

1.1         
That Cabinet approved Option 2, with the
amendments as set out in recommendation 1.2, and agreed its
implementation as soon as practically possible, and noted that this
was likely to be approximately three months following a formal
decision being made.

 

1.2         
That Sunday charging be removed from Sudbury,
Hadleigh and Pin Mill car parks, and that delegated authority be
given to the Director – Operations in consultation with the
Cabinet Member – People and Place to agree final charges at
Pin Mill. 

 
 
REASON FOR DECISION
 
Benchmarking of tariffs (Appendix B) suggested the proposals
will not exceed local market rates, which continued to place the
Councils car parks favourably where price is considered by
motorists in choosing where to park and visit. 
In
establishing the Councils approved Parking Strategy for 2022-42,
Ethos (formerly 2020 Highways and Transportation) Consultants
confirmed that the cost of parking was one of a range of
considerations when setting parking charges (see summary Appendix
E).
Data
on visits, dwell times, premises vacancies, and spending from the
three Council car park locations (see Appendix C) indicated there
has been no substantial change or significant detrimental impact on
these figures during the nine months since the revised charges were
introduced in January 2025.
The
validity of this data, which was also examined by Overview and
Scrutiny Committee in September 2025, has been qualified by the
University of Suffolk in their independent report (Appendix A). The
report concluded that ‘the introduction of parking charges
had not had a significant overall impact on these towns’,
which in turn backed up the findings of Ethos which underpin the
Councils strategy in relation to charge setting.
The
affordability of season tickets had been carefully considered to
support both residents and local workers, ensuring these tickets
remained available at a substantial discount for parking users who
had fewer options for where they can park.
A
range of ‘concessions’ continued to be provided where
appropriate and practical to operate and these would be kept under
review.
Free
parking in blue badge bays continued to be offered within all
Council owned car parks across the districts.
Free
parking options remained available in all locations, although it
was accepted at times these could be less convenient or in higher
demand.
The
planned changes would continue to support on street enforcement
which was known to improve turnover of these free
spaces.
Given the Council’s
overall MTFP budget pressures in delivering a wide range of
services for residents, it was no longer sustainable to continue
subsidising parking services without recovering full costs,
especially as further income opportunities had been thoroughly
assessed and benchmarked. If these proposals were not implemented,
equivalent reductions in other services would be necessary
instead.
 
Alternative Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Option 1 – do not
implement proposals
 
If chosen, this option would leave
a modelled total subsidy (amount adrift from full cost of service
recovery - see Appendix D) in the 2026/27 budget of
£355,626 which would have to be
found from other savings and service reductions.
 
This option is not
recommended.
 
Option 3 –
implement proposals with amendments
 
Any amendments made
could vary the overall benefit of the proposals and this would need
to be considered in respect of other identified savings elsewhere
within the Councils budgets.
 
This option is not
recommended. 
 
Any Declarations of
Interests Declared: None
Any Dispensation
Granted: None

purpose:
To seek approval for a Retrofit Advice/Cosy
Hub Advice Service
content:
It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1        
 That Cabinet approved Option 1, which
outlined a comprehensive engagement and home energy/ retrofit
advice programme, Retrofit and Energy Advice for
Communities and Households (REACH), for the benefit of residents
across the whole District.

 
1.2         That
Cabinet approved the mixture of capital and revenue budget of
£339,988 for this programme
be funded
from the Mid Suffolk Implementation reserve for the period 2025/26
to 2027/28.

 
1.3         That
Cabinet approved that the programme
be closely
aligned with the Cosy Homes initiative and for it to be
coordinated with work across housing, customer operations, and
community teams so that a  unified and efficient approach was
ensured.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
With energy bills still high by recent
historical standards, homes contributing significantly to
greenhouse gas emissions and having adequate heating and power
critical for our wellbeing, household energy efficiency and
decarbonisation
remained a national
and local priority. Households could face confusing options,
complex criteria, disparate services, and unclear pathways to
gaining support for reducing energy bills and improving the energy
efficiency of their properties.
 
This proposal responded to the specific
challenges of the District such as rural
isolation, off-gas homes, and heritage properties. It
mobilised
officers and community
champions to extend the Council’s reach, build awareness, and
accelerate uptake of energy-saving actions and the drawdown of
available funding for improving homes.
 
The Council was best placed to lead
a programme
designed to
utilise and integrate local connections,
services and capacity to greater effect through coordination and
consolidation. The dedicated resources of this programme would help simplify choices and guide
residents through their energy journey,
and enabled Mid Suffolk’s ambitions to support the
improvement of energy efficiency of homes in the district and
supported landlords and homeowners in moving towards zero-carbon
living.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
Do nothing and rely on existing local and
national provision. This option was not recommended.
 
Any Declarations of Interests
Declared: None

content:
It was
RESOLVED: -
 

1.1        
That Cabinet approved Option A and adopted the Household Recycling
and Waste Collections Policy (Appendix A) ahead of ‘Better
Recycling’ going live from June 2026.

 

1.2        
That, Cabinet agreed delegated authority for the Director of
Operations in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for Recycling
and Waste, to make technical changes to the Household Recycling and
Waste Collections Policy as required.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
The
decision to develop and adopt the proposed Household Recycling and
Waste Collection Policy was intended to standardise service
delivery across the Mid Suffolk district, ensuring consistency,
fairness, and clarity for all residents.
 
The
Policy aimed to increase recycling rates, reduce contamination, and
ensure compliance with national legislation and guidance, including
the Environment Act 2021 and the Resources and Waste Strategy for
England.
 
The
Policy also sought to provide transparency and accountability by
clearly outlining the level of service residents can expect and
their personal responsibilities in supporting effective waste
management.
 
Importantly, the Policy recognised that there would be
exceptions to the standard service, and provisions had been
included to accommodate specific needs and circumstances where
appropriate.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
OPTION B - Do nothing
This
option would not fully support the core aims of Better Recycling,
that is, to increase recycling rates and reduce waste and recycling
contamination.
 
An
outdated policy which does not reflect the current service delivery
model would not support our residents to clearly understand the
waste and recycling services that we provide and would likely lead
to sub-optimal outcomes across the service.
 
OPTION C - Postpone the approval of the Household Recycling and
Waste Collections Policy until early June 2026 when Better
Recycling goes live.
 
Whilst any delay in the Governance process would provide more
time to review and improve the Policy, it could lead to confusion
about the standards and scope for waste and recycling
services.
 
An
extensive communications campaign on Better Recycling is in
progress
and a clearly agreed policy would allow some
inevitable additional questions to be answered through having an
agreed policy position.
 
Our
waste officers would be supported by the Policy and its framework
being in place and this will offer clarity to support both
education and enforcement activities.
 
Any Declarations of Interests
Declared: None
Any Dispensation Granted: None

purpose:
To
approve the Sheltered Housing Review
content:
To
approve the Sheltered Housing Review

It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1         
Option C: That Cabinet approved the proposal to
decommission the sheltered housing service at these 2 schemes and
change the use of these units to ‘general needs’,
allocate accommodation to residents in accordance with the Gateway
to Homechoice Allocations Policy but apply a local lettings policy
(appendix 1) to be reviewed after 5 years.

 
1.2         
Schemes included in the proposal were: The Croft,
Tostock, IP30 9NX [7 Bungalows] and Manns Court, Cooks Rd,
Elmswell, IP30 9BZ [14 bungalows and 1 flat].  Total 22 homes.

 
1.3         
That delegated authority is granted to the
Director - Housing to decide upon the future use of communal spaces
and facilities, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Housing
at Mann’s Court, Elmswell. 
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
Option A is not recommended due to several reasons: there was
low uptake and demand for the current service, the costs of
replacement and maintenance of existing warden call systems would
require an increase in service charges for all tenants at the
scheme (regardless of whether they want or need the service) and
those charges would be ineligible for housing benefits impacting on
affordability.  As an alternative to
charging service charges, subsidising the install and maintenance
from the general rent pool is inequitable and the capital budget
should be prioritised to improving the decency and energy
efficiency of our homes more widely.
 
Option B was not recommended, whilst decommissioning the
sheltered housing service was supported by resident feedback and
the financial arguments, it was important to retain specified
accommodation for older persons and those with need for ground
floor and adapted bungalows/flats, and to maintain community
cohesion.
 
Option C was recommended because it ensured choice and
affordability for tenants wanting continued access to welfare
services, albeit from third-party providers rather than from the
Council.  Existing and new tenants would
not be required to pay for a service they do not need or benefit
from, and they would have greater choice and flexibility in how
they access the services.  A local
lettings policy would assure tenants that neighbouring properties
would be sensitively let and to those in need of them. 
 
Delegated authority to the Director of Housing for the communal
facility review would allow decisions to be made locally, in
consultation with residents and Cabinet Members. This approach
avoided the need to refer matters back to Cabinet, which is
time-consuming and not an efficient use of resources.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
Option A: Retain one or both schemes as sheltered housing,
replace existing systems and continue to provide services, service
charging the costs to all tenants where applicable, and/or
subsidising costs through the HRA budget. 
 
Option B: Decommission the sheltered housing service at these 2
schemes and change the use of these units to general needs, to
allocate accommodation to residents in accordance with the Gateway
to Homechoice Allocations policy with no restrictions.
 
Any Declarations of Interests Declared: None
Any Dispensation Granted: None

To

for Mid Suffolk
content:
To
approve the Biodiversity and Nature Recovery action plan and budget
for Mid Suffolk

It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1         
That Cabinet adopted Option B – and
endorsed the new approach to delivering Mid Suffolk’s
Biodiversity Action Plan for the period 2025-2028 and approved the
Biodiversity and Nature Recovery Budget to deliver this, including
the creation of a Nature Recovery Fund providing grants for
supporting action across the District.

 
1.2         
That the Biodiversity and Nature Recovery Budget
be funded from the Mid Suffolk Plan Implementation
Reserve.

 
1.3         
That Cabinet delegated responsibility for
finalising the detailed criteria of the Nature Recovery fund to the
Head of Climate and Nature Recovery in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Environment, Culture &
Wellbeing.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
The
approval of the proposed Biodiversity and Nature Recovery Budget to
deliver the Biodiversity Action Plan would demonstrate the
Council’s commitment to climate change and nature recovery,
whilst aligning with national goals and legislation. 
 
The
budget would allow more effective delivery of the actions than is
currently possible within the constraints of existing resources.
This in turn would deliver greater benefits to local biodiversity
and the district, including its residents and communities, through
increased co-benefits and engagement.
 
Providing dedicated and sufficient resource would provide the
Council and the District with a greater chance of reversing the
decline in biodiversity and habitat loss and deliver genuine nature
recovery that the biodiversity emergency required. To support
partners and other groups to build capacity and take action would ensure the greatest impact and
most efficient way of delivering our collective aims, and to
maintain progress during and beyond the lifetime of this
Biodiversity Action Plan.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Option A - the progress on the Biodiversity Action Plan be noted
without approval for additional budget.
 
Option C – the new approach to deliver ambitions in the
Biodiversity Action Plan for the period 2025-2028 is endorsed with
approval for additional budget but without a dedicated Nature
Recovery Fund.

To
approve the Abbycroft VAT Agency Model

It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1         
To amend the agreement with Abbeycroft Leisure so
that Abbeycroft Leisure becomes an agent of Babergh District
Council, this will enable the Council to adopt the HM Revenue &
Customs (HMRC) VAT changes announced in 2023.

 
1.2         
To delegate authority to the Director of Finance
& Procurement and Section 151 Officer and Abbeycroft Leisure
Ltd to implement the actions required to implement this change as
soon as possible.

 
1.3         
To delegate to the Director of Finance &
Procurement and Section 151 Officer the responsibility for
establishing budgets to reflect the revised
arrangements.

 
1.4         
To delegate to the Director of Place the annual
fee setting with Abbeycroft Leisure.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
To
ensure Babergh District Council is achieving value for money (VFM)
and operating in an efficient and legal manner.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Do
nothing and continue operating as things stand.

purpose:
To approve the Local Nature Recovery Strategy
(LNES)
content:
It was
RESOLVED: -
 
1.1         
That, Cabinet accepted Option B to approve the
Final Draft Local Nature Recovery Strategy, without
changes.
 
REASON FOR
DECISION
 
The creation and
approval of a Local Nature Recovery Strategy will demonstrate the
council’s commitment to long-term environmental
sustainability whilst aligning with national goals and
legislation.
 
The work to prepare
the LNRS has been carried out in accordance with the regulations
and statutory guidance, and all key stages of the required process
have been completed to this point.
 
Officers have
contributed collaboratively across Suffolk and Norfolk to formulate
the draft LNRSs. There have been two rounds of public consultation
and two rounds of supporting authorities’ consultation; both
contributing to the final publication.
 
The scope of the
LNRS, and the methodology used in determining its content, are to a
large extent prescribed in the statutory guidance, as well as
through several non-statutory guidance notes produced by Natural
England.
 
The public
consultation has indicated strong support for the LNRS, and the
priorities and measures within it, as well as providing further
useful feedback and information. Much of this has been taken
on-board in the Final Draft LNRS, with the themes of the main
changes set out in paragraph 9.8. Where comments have not been
taken on-board, a clear explanation for not doing so is provided in
the full consultation report.
 
Alternative
Options Considered and Rejected:
 
Option A - the
Final Draft Local Nature Recovery Strategy is not approved.
Considering the council’s current plan and prior commitment
to recognising the biodiversity emergency being faced, the option
to not approve the draft LNRS has not been proposed.
 
Option C - the
Final Draft LNRS is approved, subject to recommended changes. Note
this may cause delay to the LNRS timeline as there is limited time
between the end of this consultation and the proposed publication
date to respond to and address any requested changes.
 
Any Declarations of Interests Declared: None
Any Dispensation Granted: None
